tagline: A French company town, then down the river to Lake Tillery.
intro: From Badin, at the south end of Badin Lake, Valley Drive heads south along the Pee Dee past the turn for Morrow Mountain. A short stretch of NC 24/27/73 and then Indian Mound Road bring it into Norwood, near Lake Tillery.

Badin was a French idea. The town was established in 1913 around an aluminum plant built by the French industrialist Adrian Badin, and when the First World War stopped work on his dam, ALCOA bought it half-built and finished it. ALCOA shut the plant down in 2007, but the dams still make electricity.

moments.title: Badin
moments.text: The town's French colonial-inspired townhouses are among the earliest townhouses in North Carolina, and the Badin Historic District is on the National Register.

moments.title: Morrow Mountain State Park
moments.text: From the overlook Badin Lake lies to the north and Lake Tillery to the south, and stone quarried from this summit by early Native Americans turns up as tools from Maine to Florida.

moments.title: Lake Tillery
moments.text: When the lake was about to cover the old river bridge, the military tried dead weight, bombs and cannon fire on it, and in the end it took a ton of TNT.
